newsitem.title: UK: Dry cargo market slowing ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: Dry cargo market slowing ahead of holiday.

text.p: With the prospect of minimal chartering activity in the western world from next weekend until the new year, business reported this week has been relatively light, even for Capers which must allow longer than other vessels for subjects to be lifted.
Brokers believed the east was still steady for capers, although there were said to be signs of possible weakness for second half January onwards in the Atlantic.
Meanwhile rates for early Panamaxes in the Atlantic continued to rise.

In the South Atlantic and South East Asia conditions were said to be steady for these types, but brokers again reported a weakening market in the North Pacific where the most modern Panamaxes were understood to be fixable at down to $1,000 daily for rounds.
Handies on the continent continued in poor demand but elsewhere these types enjoyed steadier rates.

GRAIN - Brokers generally discounted the effects of the Bright Field accident in the Mississippi, saying that delays should be overcome within about a week. They reported a very active cargo line-up and plenty of grain in the pipeline.

ADM booked a 1977-built caper for 88,200 tonnes Mississippi/Holland for early Jan at a lumpsum equivalent to $13.00 basis 55'. Cargill were understood to have booked Maratha Majesty 75,000 dwt for a full cargo of grain Mississippi/Holland option UK (limited disbursements) for Dec 26/31 at a firm $14.50 (possibly upto $14.90) basis 49'.

Various rumours circulated about the US Gulf/Japan trade - Seyang were said to have fixed the NSAC-relet Daphne for 54,000 heavy grain for first half Jan at a very strong $27.50 no combo. A number of grain brokers believed this rate was above the market level.
It was said that $26.00 or $26.50 no combo had just been agreed for jan 5/18 and also that $25.20 had been fixed for second half January.

New grain orders quoted today included Toepfer with 2.2/2.6m cft US Gulf/Barcelona-Hamburg range for Jan 2/10, any size upto small Caper for barley Canadian Pacific/Saudi Arabia, and 20,000/10 heavy grain prompt Up River/India.
Saroc quote 1.2/2.5m cft grain US Gulf/Med for Dec 25/Jan 5, Garnac 16/22,000 corn plus 3/6,000 meals US Gulf/Buenaventura for Dec 27/Jan 4, and Hanjin 30,000 barley Vancouver/Qingdao for Jan 11/20.
Pacnav have a timecharter order for 36/49,000 dwt delivery US East Coast Dec 24/31 trip West Coast Mexico.
Very little has emerged about handy-size grain fixing although World Amphion 37,765 dwt was rumoured fixed by HMM from US Gulf to the Far East on private terms.

MINERALS - Caper activity was limited to a few reported fixtures and rumours that Anangel Solidarity 161,545 dwt open South Korea Dec 22 may have been fixed by Coe and Clerici for coal from Roberts Bank to Ensted.

Panamax fixtures include reports of BHP covering a prompt modern vessel delivery Far East trip via Australia to the Continent at $8,750 daily, and Gemstar fixing Mare Baltico 64,310 dwt Far East/Continent on private terms.

Stamos 63,865 dwt was linked with European charterers, possibly Interbulk, delivery S.E.Asia for 3-5 months at just over $11,000 daily. But brokers said that early Panamaxes in the Japan/S.Korea area were cutting rates.
A newbuilding Panamax was reported booked delivery Japan Dec/Jan for a North Pacific round at only $11,000 daily.
Amorgos 65,105 dwt was understood fixed by Hanjin delivery S.Korea Dec 20 for similar business at $10,500 daily.

Torm Marina 65,000 dwt was fixed by Halla in the Far East for 3-5 months at $11,500 daily but failed on subjects. In the Atlantic reports that Tatry 66,000 dwt was taken by K Line delivery Continent early Jan trip via Narvik with ironore to Cigading at $16,000 daily were inaccurate. The vessel is said to be still on subjects for this business at a significantly lower rate.
